brief: The Market Ear argues an oil-driven rise in the US 10-year yield is becoming the macro chain that matters: oil moves push yields higher, and yields should eventually hit equities, but equities have not reacted yet. The 10-year has broken above 5% into what the note calls a vacuum, trading at its most overbought level since the autumn 2022 rates panic; the next major level is 5.5%, above which the move would look less like a rates move and more like a fundamental repricing. The WTI-10-year correlation is the tightest in 35 years, and the correlation between the average US stock and the 10-year yield is the most negative since 1960. Bond and credit markets are already showing stress and bond/credit volatility has jumped while equity volatility stays depressed. The note's own view: chasing bond volatility now looks late; if bond stress spreads into a broader crisis, equities should be where the next adjustment happens, closing the gap between bond and equity vol.
